newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss minister sees Telecom flotation before 2000.
newsitem.headline: Swiss minister sees Telecom flotation before 2000.

text.p: The Swiss government aims for a partial share float of Switzerland's telecom provider before the year 2000, said Moritz Leuenberger, Swiss cabinet minister charged with liberalisation of public works.

In an interview published in Saturday's issue of "Finanz und Wirtschaft," Leuenberger said preparations were already under way to privatise 45 percent of Telecom PTT, which is to be split from the federal postal authority.

"It is my goal for us to be on the bourse before the year 2000. We are already working on the preparations. We are discussing, for example, whether we would bring the shares as one large share package of 45 percent, or in smaller, successive packages," Leuenberger said.
Leuenberger is cabinet minister for the Swiss Federal Department of Energy, Transport and Communications.
He denied that retaining the federal government as majority shareholder was a disadvantage, but also said change was possible in the future.
"We are convinced that keeping the federal government as majority shareholder is correct. But that doesn't mean that will always be the case. That can change," Leuenberger said.
He also noted Swiss law calls for the government to retain the majority, and this should calm worries among the general population that liberalisation will lead to poorer service.

The Swiss trade body representing five unions, encompassing 46,000 postal and telecom workers, has also said it is opposed to the reforms which call for reincorporating PTT Post and Telecom as separate joint stock companies.
Unions are mulling a referendum on the privatisation.

Leuenberger said he did not expect a referendum, but said that if a referendum were called, it would probably delay plans to have the new separate corporate structures for the Swiss Post and Telecom in place by the start of 1998.
That year also marks the start of liberalisation of the telecom market within the European Union.
